spans.text: The framebilt were constructed by Copehtor, the last of a previous age of similar creatures from the Old World. The framebilt are similar to golems, built from interweaving cords and roots surrounding a stone skeletal structure, all plated by metal and stone. Though they are similar to constructs they have vague approximations of a regular anatomy: they have a core that beats like a heart, muscles made of wood-like fibers that pull, stretch and grow, and nerves that feel pain.

Their purpose was originally to fill the ranks of mankind’s armies and help construct weapons during the war on the Grand Primaries, and then finally were meant to be pilots of DGR units that were to be constructed, but this never came to pass. Afterwards they became the servants of Copehtor and assistants to the Eidolons. After a certain point in history it was decided they would be put into stasis and their minds purged to prevent the construction of more DGRs or another weapon like the Sword of Damocles. As such they ended up in vaults of Copehtor across the world.

As history progressed, many were roused to consciousness by adventurers, tectonic activity, or other means. Mostly without any memory, large swathes of them reintegrated into society where they took on various new names, most forgetting the term framebilt. Some among them recalled their ancient functions: one particular framebilt, Vanderbilden, awoke with the desire to build and create, and founded the city of High Wave. Under his rule it would become the most technologically advanced city in the known world, and when discovered by outsiders he would take the role of a Retian High-Lord.

Though not constructs, the framebilt are similar to them in nature. They don’t require food, water, sleep or air, and do not age. However, the natural elements of their bodies can heal over time like regular creatures, and the same sort of damage that would kill a regular humanoid (decapitation, exsanguination, etc.), affects them just the same.

Framebilt that awaken from vaults of Copehtor are impressionable and often prone to following the orders of those who first offer them guidance. Furthermore, many who awaken don’t become fully sentient again, and are known to other framebilt as the Lockminds. Lockminds function very much as obedient drones, without much left inside to reclaim. They are still cognisant, but they lack opinions or perspective. It is not uncommon for organizations, such as the Family, to seek out vaults with the intention of creating whole troupes of Lockminds to command. Most of the framebilt stat blocks included here can be used as either, unless context clearly notes otherwise.
